hints: First name vessels A to D on this heart diagram. Look at which chamber each vessel leaves or enters.
Remember the rule: wall thickness follows blood pressure. Which vessel carries blood at the highest pressure, straight from the left ventricle to the whole body?
walkthrough:
**Identify the four vessels**

Look carefully at where each label points. A is the aorta leaving the left ventricle. D is the pulmonary artery leaving the right ventricle. B is a pulmonary vein entering the left atrium. C is a vena cava entering the right atrium.

So we have two arteries and two veins to compare.

**Apply the pressure rule**

Arteries have much thicker walls than veins because they carry blood at high pressure. They need thick smooth muscle and elastic tissue to stretch and recoil without bursting.

Between the two arteries, the aorta carries blood at much higher pressure than the pulmonary artery, because it pumps to the whole body, not just the nearby lungs.

**Pick the thickest**

The aorta withstands the highest pressure in the body, directly from the powerful left ventricle. So vessel A has the thickest wall of all.

options.A: Correct. A is the aorta. It leaves the left ventricle at the highest blood pressure, so it has the thickest muscular and elastic wall.
options.B: B is a pulmonary vein entering the left atrium. Veins are low pressure vessels with thin walls, so this is not the thickest.
options.C: C is a vena cava entering the right atrium. It carries low pressure blood back from the body, so its wall is thin.
options.D: D is the pulmonary artery. It is an artery, but it only pumps a short distance to the lungs at lower pressure than the aorta, so its wall is thinner than A.
